newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Winnie Mandela easily wins ANC post.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Winnie Mandela easily wins ANC post.

text.p: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela easily won re-election as president of South Africa's African National Congress Women's League, officials said on Sunday.

Despite speculation that President Nelson Mandela's former wife would be voted out because of her style of leadership, she beat her main opponent and deputy Thandi Modise 656-114 during a meeting of 1,000 delegates in Rustenburg in the North West province on Saturday.
A source in the ruling African National Congress (ANC) said her victory proved that she still had a strong following despite scandals that have embarrassed the party and Mandela.
"Winnie has always been a fighter and this proves that she is still popular," the source told Reuters.
"There was no serious challenge and the women have democratically chosen Winnie to lead them into the next millennium."

Political analysts said the victory meant a comeback for Madikizela-Mandela, 62, from political isolation since her 1995 divorce from Mandela who sacked her in the same year as deputy arts, culture, science and technology minister after her criticism of his unity government.
Her image continues to be scarred by the kidnap and murder of 14-year-old Stompie Seipei a year before Mandela was released in 1990 after 27 years in jail. Her bodyguard was convicted for the muder.
"If Winnie can successfully unify the Women's League and turn it into a strong voice for women, she will be back quicker than we imagined," one analyst said.
Another analysts said that she had never lost her grassroots support despite the scandals that hurt her reputation.

The nomination of Health Minister Nkosazana Dlamini Zuma, a favourite of the ANC leadership for the Women's League presidency, fizzled out at the last minute as it became clear that Madikizela-Mandela had the majority support of delegates.
The ANC on Sunday congratulated her on her re-election.
It said earlier it was concerned about the lack of unity in the league since a ban on it under apartheid was lifted in 1990.

"We believe that the leadership will work towards unity, peace and development not only within the ranks of the League, but will work with all other sectors of society to achieve these and the objectives of the reconstruction and development of our country," the ANC said in a statement.

The league's members have included such prominent women as Adelaide Tambo, widow of the late ANC president Oliver Tambo, who quit the League in 1995 in protest at Winnie's leadership, which opponents say is undemocratic.

Madikizela-Mandela has kept a low profile since her divorce from Mandela, but her re-election will guarantee her a seat on the ANC's national executive committee. She has headed the Women's League since 1993 and remains a member of parliament.
